fixes.explanation: Tribute? Friend, nobody's handing over a payment plan in this verse. Caleb doesn't negotiate with the three sons of Anak. The text says he "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" So picture Caleb showing up with no paperwork and no wallet, just moving them out (Joshua 15:14).

A treaty? Ooh, that's a very polite guess, baker. Very civilized. Pens out, tea on the table. But no pens in this verse. It says Caleb "…drove out from there the three sons of Anak…" and the three are named: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. Caleb doesn't sign anything, he moves them out (Joshua 15:14).

How long she'll stay? Ha, you've got Caleb checking the calendar like a host who wants to know when the guests are leaving. Not this dad, baker. When Acsah gets off her donkey, he asks, "What do you desire?" He's asking what she wants, and I think that's a dad leaning in to listen (Joshua 15:18).

True, baker! Acsah asks for springs of water, and Caleb doesn't hold back. The verse says "So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs." She asked, and she got the upper and the lower. I think that's a dad who loves saying yes (Joshua 15:19).
